title: HttpRequest
description: Types the data payload flowing through HTTP Effectors/Receptors when the payload is an HTTP request message. Extending archetypes add domain-specific body shapes and additional headers via $ref/allOf composition. Source: RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics, 2022), §3.4 — Messages; RFC 9112 (HTTP/1.1, 2022), §3 — Request Line.

method.description: HTTP request method. GET — retrieve a representation of the target resource (§9.3.1). HEAD — same as GET but without response body (§9.3.2). POST — process a representation subordinate to the target resource (§9.3.3). PUT — replace the target resource state entirely (§9.3.4). PATCH — partially modify the target resource state (RFC 5789). DELETE — remove the target resource (§9.3.5). OPTIONS — describe communication options for the target resource (§9.3.7). Source: RFC 9110 §9.

targetUri.description: URI template identifying the target resource (e.g., '/api/users/{id}'). Resolved at runtime with concrete values. Source: RFC 6570 (URI Template, 2012); RFC 9110 §7.1 — Determining the Target Resource.

contentType.description: Media type of the request payload body (IANA media type, e.g., 'application/json'). Source: RFC 9110 §8.3 — Content-Type; RFC 6838 — Media Type Specifications.

accept.description: Media type(s) acceptable in the response, for content negotiation (e.g., 'application/json', 'text/html;q=0.9, application/json'). Supports quality-value syntax. Source: RFC 9110 §12.5.1 — Accept.

body.description: Request message content. At protocol level, unconstrained; extending archetypes constrain this to a domain-specific shape via $ref/allOf composition. Source: RFC 9110 §6.4 — Content.
